headline: AI memory boom drives record revenue and margins higher
summary_short: Micron's fiscal Q3 2026 (labeled FY2026 Q2 on this shard) revenue rocketed 345.7% y/y and 73.7% q/q to $41.46 billion, with GAAP diluted EPS of $24.67 as gross margin expanded to 84.6% from 37.7% a year ago on surging AI-driven memory demand.
summary_long: Revenue rose 345.7% y/y and 73.7% q/q to $41.46B on broad-based AI-driven memory demand, led by Cloud Memory ($13.77B, more than doubled q/q) and Core Data Center ($11.52B, up over 100% q/q); all four business units posted double-digit operating-margin expansion. GAAP gross margin expanded to 84.6% from 37.7% y/y and operating margin to 80.4% from 23.3%, driving net income to $28.24B and diluted EPS to $24.67. Operating cash flow was $25.39B and adjusted free cash flow $18.3B; cash and equivalents rose to $25.0B from $13.9B. Micron declared a $0.15/share dividend and guided FQ4 2026 revenue to $50.0B±$1.0B and GAAP diluted EPS to $30.73±$1.00, tied to new multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements.

drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based across all four business units, led by Cloud Memory ($13.77B, up from $7.75B) and Core Data Center ($11.52B, up from $5.69B), as AI-driven memory demand accelerated.
Margin expansion is explained by cost of goods sold rising only 4.8% q/q while revenue rose 73.7% q/q, consistent with the segment-level margin gains disclosed across all four business units.
Operating expenses rose just 7.3% q/q against 73.7% revenue growth, so operating income scaled almost directly with the gross-margin expansion.
EPS growth tracked net-income growth almost one-for-one; diluted share count was roughly flat (1,145M vs 1,142M q/q), so buybacks were not a material driver this quarter.

CEO Sanjay Mehrotra attributed results to "the strategic value of memory in the AI era" and said new multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements will enhance the durability and predictability of future performance.
